Capital Seasons Map

Which season each state capital is in by your temperature rules, updated every morning with a 10-day forecast and a rough 6-month outlook. Drag the slider to move through the year.

The rules

  • Spring starts on the 3rd straight day with a high of 55°F or more. Counting begins Mar 1.
  • Summer starts on the 5th straight day with a high of 75°F or more. Counting begins May 15.
  • Autumn starts on the first night with a low under 50°F. Counting begins Sep 1.
  • Winter starts on the first night with a low under 28°F. Counting begins Nov 1.

Only days on or after the start of counting count toward a streak. There is no deadline: a season keeps waiting for its conditions until the next season arrives first, and then it is skipped for that year.

Forecast outlines: likely means the forecast clears the rule by 3°F or more and the change is 3 days out or less. Anything else close to qualifying, including near misses within 3°F, is possible.

Start dates

“Skipped” means the next season’s conditions arrived first, so the capital never entered that season that year.
